item.title: JAMA
JAMA Editors' Summary Podcast September 18, 2026
item.description: Listen to the JAMA Editor’s Summary for an overview and discussion of the important articles appearing in JAMA.

item.title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Advanced Pancreatic Cancer
item.description: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a first-in-class therapy for patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer.

item.title: Mpox Virus Transitions Toward Endemicity
item.description: Surveillance data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) suggest that the clade IIb mpox virus is transitioning toward endemic circulation.

item.title: FDA Approves 2 New Alzheimer Disease Blood Tests
item.description: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved 2 new blood tests to detect Alzheimer disease in adults with cognitive symptoms, including 1 for those as young as 40 years old.

item.title: Earlier Menopause Linked to Faster Cognitive Decline
item.description: Earlier age at menopause may be associated with faster cognitive decline, a study published in JAMA Network Open suggests.

item.title: How Do Cardiovascular Risks Vary Across Nicotine Products?
item.description: Although cigarette smoking is the most harmful form of nicotine use, all nicotine-containing products produce adverse cardiovascular effects, according to a recent review.

item.title: Updated Stroke Guideline Emphasizes Early, Holistic Intervention
item.description: Stroke rehabilitation should start as early as possible and address personalized physical, cognitive, language, and emotional needs, according to an updated 2026 guideline from the American Heart Association and the American Stroke Association.

item.title: Why More Adults Are Being Diagnosed With ADHD
item.description: This Medical News article discusses the rise in adults seeking attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) evaluations and the need for more consistent approaches to diagnosis and treatment as primary care clinicians take on a larger role.

item.title: The Latest on Caffeine and Heart Health
item.description: This Medical News article discusses a recent scientific statement from the American Heart Association about caffeine and cardiovascular disease.

item.title: Characteristics of Patients Choosing Intravenous Moderate Sedation for IUD Placement
item.description: This study examined the prevalence of intravenous moderate sedation (IVS) for intrauterine device (IUD) placement when universally offered, as well as the demographic, reproductive, and social factors associated with its use.

item.title: Floating
item.description: In this narrative medicine essay, an infectious diseases physician’s childhood memories of falling, fleeing, and floating serve as metaphors of grieving her mother’s death.

item.title: Lasker Winners’ Work Leads to New Narcolepsy Treatment
item.description: This Medical News article is an interview with Emmanuel Mignot, MD, PhD, and Masashi Yanagisawa, MD, PhD, winners of the 2026 Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award for their identification of the neuropeptide orexin and its role in narcolepsy.

item.title: Error in Results
item.description: The Original Investigation titled “Adjuvant Nivolumab vs Observation in Resected Non–Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial,” published on June 1, 2026, was corrected to fix typographical errors in the text, including indicating that the trial was stopped for futility at 75% information, rather than 78%, and the number of participants lost to follow-up in the nivolumab group in Figure 1. This article was corrected online.

item.description: Dana L. Farnsworth, M.D., Cambridge, Mass.

item.title: Digitalis Glycosides in Patients With Heart Failure
item.description: To the Editor A recent meta-analysis of 3 large placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials suggested a lower risk of cardiovascular death or first worsening heart failure (HF) event in patients with HF who were treated with digitalis glycosides. However, several important limitations warrant particular consideration.

item.title: Digitalis Glycosides in Patients With Heart Failure—Reply
item.description: In Reply We appreciate the letter from Dr Čulić about our meta-analysis, which showed that treatment with digitalis glycosides was associated with a significant 20% relative risk reduction in the primary outcome of cardiovascular death and HF hospitalization, mainly attributable to a lower risk of HF hospitalizations.

item.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis in Adults: A Review
item.description: This Review discusses the pathogenesis, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

item.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
item.description: To the Editor Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) remains one of the most common and treatable causes of dizziness encountered in clinical practice. We enjoyed the recently published JAMA Insights article on the treatment of BPPV and the associated JAMA Patient Page on BPPV. The Epley maneuver has appropriately become the default therapeutic approach for posterior canal BPPV, given its ease of use, robust evidence base, and broad adoption across specialties. However, the near-universal reliance on the Epley maneuver risks narrowing clinician awareness of equally effective and, in some contexts, potentially advantageous alternatives such as the Semont-plus maneuver.

item.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo—Reply
item.description: In Reply Regarding our recent JAMA Insights about the treatment of BPPV, Dr Purks and colleagues question our decision not to advocate for integrating the use of the Semont-plus maneuver into routine practice. We offer 2 points in response.
